checks: The threshold sign is correct with theta=(a,-b), so the constraint derivative is B δu+G δtheta. For proper sections the Fréchet cap variation has positive enlarging sign and coarea factor 1/|u|.

At a zero-area supporting section, the perturbation is contained in a slab of thickness O(parameter change) whose section-area supremum tends to zero. Multiplication by bounded q or x retains the little-o estimate. Strictly separated traces are locally constant. In d=1 a nonempty supporting point has counting measure one and is excluded by the zero-measure assumption.

The assumed moment continuity gives continuously differentiable constraint and objective moment maps; G invertible gives local exact mass and base balance by the implicit function theorem. The feasible cap maximizes via the affine-score sign and both moment constraints, so no global dual-attainment assumption enters.

The first-derivative boundary term with u·x is minus the term with theta·q on the active section, which vanishes by the constrained derivative. Differentiating the resulting gradient produces E-B^T G^{-1}B divided by t. The square completes with c=-G^{-1}Bv, and for v=u the old theta makes the integrand identically zero.
Checked original b4c3b9c6a52059d2 §5, (12)–(14). This is the support of a fixed balanced moment body, not a Hessian of the ambient depth.

dependencies.hypotheses: In each proper positive fiber translate from a point of its section in the fiber interior, divide by |u| to use the unit-normal proper-cut column argument, and take the continuous bounded coordinate weights q or x in the original coordinates. Multiplying by fiber volume removes the normalized-measure convention.

Use the local geometric slab estimate in §2 of the proof for each supporting trace with zero section area. Its weighted consequence follows by boundedness of q and x on the finite compact sampled family. The projected-contact assumptions of the main theorem are not invoked.

overlap.comparison: Provides the proper-section cap differential and a one-body fixed-mass support Hessian at a centered section. It does not retain all base-balance moments or their Schur complement.
Provides zero-tangency first variation at a cap, not implicit persistence of a base-balanced cap or the support Hessian.

readability: The order-two continuity assumption covers q–q, q–x and x–x section moments and supplies precisely the C¹ input to the implicit function theorem.
review_method: Independent proof read, predecessor-scope and provenance check, and exact rational replay where needed
summary: The coarea matrices give the claimed support Hessian under the stated regularity and positive-definite constraint block.
